issue_context.title: [API Proposal]: Additional Regex.EnumerateMatches/Count overloads
comments:
Tagging subscribers to this area: @dotnet/area-system-text-regularexpressions See info in [area-owners.md](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/area-owners.md) if you want to be subscribed.
Issue Details
### Background and motivation The existing Regex.Matches method has an overload that accepts an `int startat`, but the newly added `EnumerateMatches` method lacks such an overload. While you can slice the input span to begin at some position into the input, there's a difference in regex between "beginning" and "starting". The former means there's no available input prior to where the matching process first runs, whereas the latter means there may be available input prior to where the matching process first runs. That's relevant for lookbehinds, as a lookbehind can see text prior to a "startat" but not prior to a "beginning". And it means uses like: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ed2472b72679ff5ca0fa56996cf15d2fc303c7db/src/libraries/System.Private.Xml/src/System/Xml/XmlConvert.cs#L195-L200 which could otherwise shift to using `EnumerateMatches` for a performance gain are unable to do so, as this particular case has a lookbehind and uses a potentially positive startat value. ### API Proposal ```diff public class Regex { + public Regex.ValueMatchEnumerator EnumerateMatches(System.ReadOnlySpan input, int startat); } ``` ### API Usage ```csharp foreach (ValueMatch m in _regex.EnumerateMatches(input, startat)) { ... } ``` ### Alternative Designs _No response_ ### Risks _No response_

Sounds good to me. I did consider adding this as well to match other APIs, but didn't because I saw that slicing would be a workaround, but I do see your point about lookbehinds is valid, so I agree this should be added..
Should `startat` be camel case? i.e `startAt`? Or is it being left as the existing API's have it named this way?

> Or is it being left as the existing API's have it named this way?

Right, I was being consistent with the existing parameters casing.

review_comments: Good catch! I would have expected tests to catch this, but I'm glad you now added tests for it 👍
Just curious, why is this preferred than `int count = 0;`?

Doesn't really matter either way.  I'd separated it when I had multiple similar blocks and wanted them all to be consistent in terms of setting count to 0, and it felt inconsistent having one of them declare the varaible.
